passages.source_excerpt: p. 228: "some Phoenician divine names as Mlqrt, “Melqart”, from milk (“king”) + qart (“city”), or 'štr'sy, from 'štrt (“Astarte”) and 'sy (“Isis”), belong to this category". p. 196: "A similar development gave rise to the divine name Mlqrt < *milk qart, “the king of the City”, and to mlkty < *milk Kitti, “king of Kition”." p. 188: "in the Phoenician name of the god mlqrt < *milk-qart, “the king of the city”".
passages.passage_support: Directly substantiates the naming leg of the tested claim from the very work the designated tertiary page relays: the comparative grammar itself derives Mlqrt from milk 'king' + qart 'city' and glosses it 'king of the City'. The god is cited in this grammar only in those three technical passages — as a phonological/morphological example (assimilation, sandhi-spelling, blended nouns) — not as a merchandising figure; the book has no theological profile of Melqart to offer or withhold.
passages.edition_caveat: The digitised copy is the 1997 first edition (754/756 pp.). The passage content itself is verified in the 1997 text at the three locations above.

passages.priority: peer-reviewed scholarly fulltext (second-hand witness to the book)
passages.label: Jourdain-Annequin's review of Bonnet 1988 — the book's thesis and page-anchored quotations
passages.source_citation: Colette Jourdain-Annequin, compte-rendu of "Studia Phoenicia VIII. Melqart. Cultes et mythes de l'Héraclès tyrien en Méditerranée par Corinne Bonnet, 1988 (Bibliothèque de la Faculté de Philosophie et lettres de Namur 69)", Revue des Études Anciennes 92 (1990), no. 3–4, pp. 446–449. The review states the book is "issu d'une thèse soutenue à Liège en 1987" and describes it as "un recensement exhaustif et critique des testimonia relatifs aux cultes et aux mythes de Melqart dans le bassin méditerranéen".
passages.source_kind: peer-reviewed book review; fulltext served as per-page text (Persée), fetched page by page (?pageId=T1_446…449)
passages.source_locator: p. 446 (historiography list + n. 1); p. 447 (BIBLIOGRAPHIE 447 — review's assessment); p. 448 (quotes Bonnet 1988 pp. 417, 421, 431, 436); p. 449 (quote of Bonnet 1988 p. 432)
passages.source_excerpt: p. 447: “Nous disposons donc désormais d'un recensement exhaustif et critique des testimonia relatifs aux cultes et aux mythes de Melqart dans le bassin méditerranéen et, sur cette base, pour la première fois réunie, l'auteur — confortée par une abondante bibliographie — construit une synthèse claire et intelligente”. p. 448: “«Melqart est, en terre phénicienne, l'avatar stricto sensu d'une lignée d'ancêtres royaux divinisés» propose l'auteur (p. 417)”; “le Baal de Tyr s'affirmant alors comme «l'expression culminante de ce phénomène de la religion urbaine» (p. 431)”. p. 449: “il concentrait entre ses mains «un éventail toujours plus large de prérogatives» (p. 432)”.
passages.passage_support: Supports the civic-semantics leg against the book the entry cites: an independent specialist reviewer reports the 1988 monograph's thesis as dynastic-royal and urban — Melqart as avatar of a line of divinized royal ancestors, the Baal of Tyre as the culminating expression of urban religion, with the Greek Heracles assimilation as a staged, later development. Nothing in the review frames Melqart's defining job as patronage of merchants. It also verifies the entry's bibliographic anchor (author, title, Studia Phoenicia 8, Peeters 1988, Liège thesis 1987) at book level, though the book's own pages were not opened.
passages.note: Quotations are transcribed from the page text as Persée serves it (hidden OCR text layer for the scanned review pages), including its bracketed insertions; they are page-anchored to Bonnet 1988 via the review's own citations. The reviewer is a Heracles specialist (author of a thesis on Heracles); the review is not a relay of the designated tertiary source.

basis: Scholarly-fulltext escalation against the R8-F04 residual hold. (1) Naming leg — now read at source: the grammar the designated tertiary page relays states the derivation itself, three times, in its own text (printed pp. 188, 196, 228 of the 1997 edition: mlqrt < *milk(-)qart, 'the king of the city' / 'the king of the City'; and the index lists Mlqrt only under those two sections). The relayed-page gap from round 8 ('Lipiński's page remains unread') is therefore closed in content, with a stated edition/pagination caveat for the literal 'p. 235'. (2) Attribution leg — Bonnet 1988 is now witnessed at book level by an independent peer-reviewed review (REA 92/1990) that reports the monograph as a thesis-based exhaustive testimonia dossier on Melqart and quotes it page-anchored (pp. 417, 421, 431, 432, 436) with a dynastic-royal and urban-profile thesis — civic semantics, not a merchant job — and by Bonnet's own 2009 chapter calling Melqart 'dieu poliade de Tyr' and naming the 1988 book 'ma synthèse'. (3) Anti-fixing leg — supported as calibrated absence over this session's set (zero commercial-role framing in the review's four pages; none in the 2009 chapter's framing; none in the grammar), consistent with round 8's finding that only the Aubet relay inside the tertiary page carries the trader-protector wording. The tested sentence itself is unchanged since the round-8 admit commit (empty git diff against e1694ba…).
limits: 1) The 1988 monograph's own pages remain UNREAD as a book: the thesis and its page-anchored quotations reach me through a review whose text is Persée's OCR layer, i.e. a second-hand witness — strong for the book's existence, thesis and profile-shape, not a substitute for the book. 2) The Wikipedia relay's "Lipiński 2002, p. 235" is not verified: the copy read is the 1997 first edition, which prints the etymology at pp. 188/196/228; the second edition (2001/2002, 780 pp.) was not reachable this session (Google Books quota). Literal page 235 → `to-verify`. 3) The Lipiński copy read is a third-party unauthorised digitisation from a personal upload path; no publisher-authorised copy was opened. Rights/attribution rulings are out of this lane's province and are reported to the parent, not absorbed. 4) Bonnet 2009 quotations are vision transcriptions from image-only pages (crop sha256s recorded); a glyph-level error is possible in diacritics even where the sentence reading is unambiguous. 5) The reviewer's 1990 evaluation is not the book: its silence about commercial roles is weaker evidence than the book's own silence would be. 6) HathiTrust coverage of the book remains unchecked (403), so the negative-fulltext claim is statement-limited to the routes actually probed. 7) The round-8 WiBiLex author-line limit was not re-attempted (out of this hunt's focus).
coupling_implication: Direction unchanged, now better anchored at source: for a fiction system, the city-god role is the primary attested frame for Melqart (name, poliadic cult, royal-house and urban-religion profile, colonial expansion), while commercial protection is at best one late, locally variable function (Aubet relay) and must never be the definition; Greek Heracles equivalence is staged late (review quoting Bonnet 1988 p. 436), i.e. a translation instrument, not biography transfer. Downstream: keep the entry's hedges ('understood as', 'more productive than') and keep the '(Bonnet 1988)' attribution, which now resolves to a real, author-acknowledged monograph — but do not quote Bonnet 1988 by page without the book in hand.
